canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both reviewers' activation and lower-band blockers remain supported after code/spec verification. Reviewer 1's single lower-band blocker and Reviewer 2's two lower-band blockers describe the same surviving end-to-end gap, so the canonical review merges them into one critical finding covering both the empty chunk-reader fallback and the pass-through/carry-forward lower-band composition path. The reviewers disagreed on the missing workbench integration/E2E suites; the test plan plus a fresh `npm run verify-all` run show those suites are still absent, so that blocker is retained. Reviewer 1's chunk-derived turn-placement concern was not confirmed because the current epic and tech-design artifacts do not explicitly require mapping chunk `sourceTurnIds` back into turn relationship hints.
crossStoryFindings: Story 5 lower-band awareness never becomes a real production dependency of Stories 2 and 6: readiness/detail rely on injected chunk data, while draft editing and materialization can persist lower-band selections without proving real chunk eligibility or summary availability.
Story 6 activation breaks the shared source-safety seam established by Context Steward because it rewrites `thread.json` from a stale snapshot outside the canonical ThreadStore mutation queue.
The epic gate is green, but the required Context Workbench integration and E2E suites are absent, so cross-story filesystem seams for query, search, edit, and activate were not exercised end to end.
architectureFindings: The tech design says lower-band reads come from persisted chunk lifecycle/artifact state and the materializer accepts chunk inputs, but the implementation ships no production chunk reader and omits chunk inputs from the materializer contract.

Canonical thread metadata writes are architected behind `ThreadStore.updateThreadMetadata` and `FileThreadStore.globalThreadQueues`, but `FileThreadViewStore.activateThreadView` bypasses that boundary with a direct `thread.json` rewrite.
The deep-gate architecture promised `tests/context-workbench/*.integration.test.ts` and `tests/context-workbench/*.e2e.test.ts` suites; only context-steward deep suites exist.

productionPathFindings: `WorkbenchQueryService` falls back to `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER`, so lower-band readiness and chunk detail only function when a caller injects chunk data; the repo's only concrete reader lives in a unit test.

`ThreadViewEditService.updateThreadViewBands` accepts lower-band records by pass-through clone, and `ThreadViewMaterializer` carries forward stored detailed/brief messages instead of resolving selected chunks into emitted summaries.
`FileThreadViewStore.activateThreadView` reads a Thread snapshot and rewrites the whole `thread.json` directly, creating a stale-write path outside `FileThreadStore`'s canonical mutation queue.

blockingFindings.title: Activation can clobber live thread metadata because it bypasses the canonical thread-store mutation queue
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/context-workbench/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:396-476` runs activation under `FileThreadViewStore.threadMutationQueues` (`:84`, `:549-576`), reads the current Thread via `threadStore.openThread` (`:402-405`), clones that snapshot, mutates only `activeThreadViewId` and `updatedAt` (`:462-464`), and rewrites the whole `thread.json` directly (`:475`). Canonical Thread metadata writes otherwise go through `threadStore.updateThreadMetadata` and `FileThreadStore.globalThreadQueues` (`src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:369-476`, `:580-601`). A concurrent import, append, repair, or metadata update can therefore land after the snapshot read and be lost when activation writes the stale full-file snapshot.

blockingFindings.title: Lower-band read and composition paths are still test-shimmed instead of production-backed
blockingFindings.evidence: `WorkbenchQueryService` defaults to `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER` (`src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:115-119`, `:275-280`), and the only concrete `listChunks` implementation in the repo is the test-only `InMemoryChunkReader` (`tests/context-workbench/workbench-query-service.test.ts:85-92`, `:527-530`). On the write path, `ThreadViewEditService.updateThreadViewBands` clones caller-supplied `detailedBand` and `briefBand` records without validating chunk ids or `sourceUnitType` (`src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-edit-service.ts:300-305`, `:324-325`), while `ThreadViewMaterializer` validates only turn bands (`src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:231-258`, `:378-387`) and merely carries forward existing detailed/brief emitted messages (`:260-270`, `:403-409`) instead of resolving selected chunks into `detailed_chunk_summary` or `brief_chunk_summary` outputs. This conflicts with the lower-band flow and materialization contracts in `docs/spec-build/epics/02-context-workbench/tech-design.md:516-525` and `:686-703`, leaving Story 5 behavior functional only through injected test data or pre-seeded emitted messages.

blockingFindings.title: Required Context Workbench integration and E2E suites are missing, so `verify-all` does not exercise the feature's real seams
blockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/02-context-workbench/test-plan.md:221-242` requires `tests/context-workbench/file-thread-view-store.integration.test.ts` and `tests/context-workbench/context-workbench.e2e.test.ts` with 4 integration and 9 E2E cases, and `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:31-47` only runs files ending in `.integration.test.ts` or `.e2e.test.ts` for those modes. The repo currently contains only `tests/context-steward/file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` and `tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts`. A fresh `npm run verify-all` run passed by executing those context-steward deep suites, so no Context Workbench filesystem-backed deep-gate coverage exists despite the test-plan requirement.

unresolvedItems: Reviewer 1's concern that turn search/detail hides chunk-backed participation was not confirmed in this pass: `src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:181-199` and `src/context-workbench/services/workbench-search-service.ts:328-341` only surface direct `turn`-band placements, but the current epic and tech-design artifacts do not explicitly require mapping chunk `sourceTurnIds` back into turn relationship hints.

Fixing the lower-band production path still needs a concrete decision on where Feature 2 reads real chunk lifecycle and summary artifacts from, because the codebase currently exposes only the `WorkbenchChunkReader` interface and a test-local `InMemoryChunkReader`.

architectureFindings: The tech design says lower-band readiness should read real chunk lifecycle and summary artifacts, but the implementation has no production chunk reader and no lower-band materializer.
The architecture isolates canonical Thread writes behind `FileThreadStore` queueing, but activation in `FileThreadViewStore` bypasses that boundary and writes `thread.json` directly.
Turn relationship APIs drifted after lower-band chunks were added: search/detail only report placements for bands whose `sourceUnitType` is `turn`, so chunk-backed participation is invisible.

productionPathFindings: `WorkbenchQueryService` falls back to `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER`, which returns no chunks unless a caller injects a custom reader; the only concrete reader in the repo is the test-only `InMemoryChunkReader`.
Lower-band emitted messages are not assembled from source artifacts in production code; they are only carried forward if they were already stored on the Thread View record.
Activation writes `thread.json` directly from a cloned snapshot, creating a stale-write production path outside the canonical `FileThreadStore` mutation queue.

blockingFindings.title: Activation can clobber live source-thread metadata because it bypasses the canonical mutation queue
blockingFindings.evidence: `FileThreadViewStore.activateThreadView` reads a thread snapshot, mutates only `activeThreadViewId`/`updatedAt`, and writes the whole `thread.json` back directly (`src/context-workbench/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:402-475`) while using its own `threadMutationQueues` (`src/context-workbench/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:553-576`). Canonical thread writes serialize through a different `FileThreadStore.globalThreadQueues` path (`src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:369-417`, `src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:580-601`). A concurrent append/import/repair/turn write can therefore land after the snapshot read and then be overwritten by activation's stale full-file rewrite, violating the source-safety contract.

blockingFindings.title: Lower-band behavior is backed by test-only shims instead of a real chunk production path
blockingFindings.evidence: The only default chunk path is `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER`, which always returns `[]` (`src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:115-119`, `src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:275-280`), and the only concrete reader in the repo is the test-local `InMemoryChunkReader` (`tests/context-workbench/workbench-query-service.test.ts:85-107`). `ThreadViewEditService.updateThreadViewBands` accepts `detailedBand`/`briefBand` by raw clone without validating chunk ids or source unit type (`src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-edit-service.ts:300-305`, `src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-edit-service.ts:324-325`). `ThreadViewMaterializer` never builds lower-band messages from chunk summaries; it only carries forward previously stored lower-band emitted messages (`src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:260-269`, `src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:403-425`). That means Story 5 lower-band readiness/composition is not a real execution path.

blockingFindings.title: The epic gate passes without any Context Workbench integration or E2E coverage
blockingFindings.evidence: The test plan requires `file-thread-view-store.integration.test.ts` and `context-workbench.e2e.test.ts` with 4 integration and 9 E2E cases (`docs/spec-build/epics/02-context-workbench/test-plan.md:221-242`, `docs/spec-build/epics/02-context-workbench/test-plan.md:248-253`). `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs` only includes files ending in `.integration.test.ts` or `.e2e.test.ts` for those modes (`scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:31-47`). There are no such files under `tests/context-workbench`, so the passing `npm run verify-all` in this review exercised only the existing Context Steward deep suites and never validated workbench filesystem-backed activation, search, or lower-band seams.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Turn search/detail hides chunk-backed Thread View participation
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Both turn-detail placements and turn-search relationship hints only report bands whose `sourceUnitType` is `turn` (`src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:181-199`, `src/context-workbench/services/workbench-search-service.ts:328-341`). Once detailed/brief bands are chunk-based, a turn represented through a selected chunk will appear to have no active/draft view relationship, which drifts from the Story 2 detail/search contracts after Story 5 added chunk-backed lower bands.

crossStoryFindings: The implemented Context Workbench module set is broadly coherent across stories: domain records, file-backed Thread View store, query/search/edit/materialize/compare/activation services, and service tests are present and generally align for AC-1 through AC-5 and AC-7.

Cross-story drift appears around lower-band awareness/composition: query tests inject chunk data, but edit/materialization paths can persist lower-band selections without proving the selected chunks are real, closed, or artifact-ready.
architectureFindings: Thread Views are implemented as first-class persisted records under `threads/<thread-id>/thread-views/<thread-view-id>/thread-view.json`, with active/draft/archived state and an active pointer on the source Thread, matching the core persistence architecture.

The architecture contract that lower bands use closed chunk selections only is not enforced at the edit/materialization boundary. `ThreadViewEditService.updateThreadViewBands` clones `detailedBand` and `briefBand` inputs directly, and `ThreadViewMaterializer` validates only upper-band turn selections.

The workbench query service exposes a `WorkbenchChunkReader` boundary, but its production default is an empty reader rather than a real file-backed/maintenance-backed artifact reader, so lower-band readiness depends on test injection instead of a real execution path.
epicCoverageAssessment: AC-1 through AC-5 and AC-7 appear materially covered by service implementation and passing unit tests.

AC-6 is incomplete in production behavior: detailed/brief bands can be represented as chunk selections in records, but the production path does not enforce closed-chunk eligibility or real artifact availability when editing/materializing a Thread View.

The test plan requires dedicated Context Workbench integration and E2E suites for realistic Thread View persistence/workbench lifecycle seams, but no `tests/context-workbench/*.integration.test.ts` or `tests/context-workbench/*.e2e.test.ts` files are present.
productionPathFindings: Material finding: `WorkbenchQueryService` defaults to `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER`, which returns `okWorkbenchResult([])`. Any production construction that omits an injected chunk reader silently reports no chunks and cannot expose lower-band readiness from real artifacts.

Material finding: lower-band edit/materialization uses pass-through/carry-forward behavior rather than a real chunk artifact path. `updateThreadViewBands` accepts `detailedBand`/`briefBand` directly, while the materializer carries forward existing lower-band emitted messages instead of resolving selected chunks to detailed/brief summaries.

blockingFindings.title: Lower-band selections are persisted without closed-chunk or artifact validation
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-edit-service.ts:304` and `:324-325` clone caller-provided `detailedBand`/`briefBand` into the next view and update patch without checking chunk existence, `sourceUnitType`, lifecycle status, or summary readiness. `src/context-workbench/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:231-258` validates only turn selections, and `:260-266` carries forward existing lower-band messages rather than resolving selected chunks.

blockingFindings.title: Lower-band production path uses an empty chunk reader fallback
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/context-workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:115-119` defines `EMPTY_CHUNK_READER` returning an empty chunk list, and the service constructor uses it as the default. This means `inspectLowerBandReadiness` and `openChunkDetail` only work with injected test data unless a real chunk reader is explicitly wired.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Context Workbench deep-gate suites required by the test plan are missing
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/02-context-workbench/test-plan.md:221-242` requires `file-thread-view-store.integration.test.ts` and `context-workbench.e2e.test.ts` coverage, and `:248-253` expects 4 integration plus 9 E2E tests for Feature 2. The repo currently has only unit-style files under `tests/context-workbench/`; `npm run verify-all` passed by running existing `tests/context-steward` integration/e2e suites.

unresolvedItems: Need an architectural decision or implementation for where real chunk lifecycle and summary artifacts are read from in Feature 2, so the `WorkbenchChunkReader` can be wired without test-only injection.
